1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the State Respondents, Sri Sarvesh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel appearing for the National Highways Authority of India and Sri Rakesh Maurya, Advocate, who has filed memo of appearance on behalf of the respondent no.4.
2.

This petition has been filed with the following main prayers:-
"(i) To issue a writ, order or direction the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned orders dated 11.01.2024 and 13.02.2024 passed by the opposite party no.3 which are contained in a Annexure No.3, 4 and 6 to this writ petition respectively.

Ram Bahadur And Others vs National Highways Authority Of India ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120343902/
1 (ii) to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the opposite party No.3 to refer the matter to the Arbitrator as provided under Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 for the determination of the compensation of the assets which are sought to be acquired from Gata No.31 and Gata No.5 situated at Village- Bhatehari, Pargana- Salon, Tehsil- Unchahar, District- Raebareli."

sentences.text: 3. We have gone through the impugned orders dated 11.01.2024 and 13.02.2024 and we find that on the basis of some complaint made by the petitioners, an enquiry was carried out and for the said enquiry after going through the Award that has already been declared on the land in question,
information

has been sent by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Raebareli to the District Magistrate Raebareli saying that the Award as determined compensation for construction, which the complainant has already received.
Similarly, in the report dated 11.01.2024, the Special Land Acquisition Officer has informed on the basis of the Award passed that compensation has already been received by the complainants.
4. The petitioner has not challenged the Award.
Till date, the petitioner has only made the application dated 03.02.3024 to the District Magistrate, a copy of which has been filed as annexure-5 to the petition.
The District Magistrate in a routine manner has marked it to the Special Land Acquisition Officer saying that the complaint be looked into and appropriate remedy be given.
This application is not under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
5. It has been informed by Sri Sarvesh Kumar Dubey to this Court that the Award has not been annexed in this petition, but he has instructions to say that Award was passed some time in the year 2018.
There is a limitation of three years.
He has also referred to Section 3G(5) and 3G(6) of the Act.
6. The Award admittedly was passed in 2022 and limitation to challenge it has not expired.
7. We dispose of this writ petition with a direction to the petitioner to file his application under Section 3G(5) within a week.
It shall be considered in accordance with law and decided expeditiously by the Competent Authority within four months from the receipt of the same.
